title: Hemodynamic effects of neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) compared to conventional ventilation modes in children after cardiac surgery
summary: This study aims to investigate how a specialized form of ventilation – known as neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) – affects the circulatory system and vital functions in children following cardiac surgery, compared to conventional mechanical ventilation. The study will examine whether the use of NAVA can lead to improved cardiovascular stability and a faster recovery in pediatric patients.

interventions.name:
Comparison of neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) with conventional ventilation modes, such as assisted and controlled ventilation, in terms of hemodynamic stability, improved cardiac function, optimized cerebral and renal perfusion, and reduced stress levels in pediatric patients
